findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There were various Time/Temperature control (TCS) foods stored inside of the prep cooler that were probed between 45F - 50F. These items included salads, mayonnaise, cheeses, meats, and dressings. The PIC mentioned that the cooler had recently been restocked at 1:30pm after lunch. The facility was instructed to place bulk items back into the walk in cooler and to use time control for the items at the top of the cooler. The facility will discard items after four hours. Ensure that TCS foods are held at 41F or below. Will follow up on July 6, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The prep cooler had an ambient temperature of 50F. See violation #22 for further details. Ensure that the prep cooler is sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. Will follow up on July 6, 2026 to see that the cooler has been serviced or replaced.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: The service prep cooler did not contain an internal thermometer to measure the ambient temperature. Discussed with the PIC. Ensure that an internal thermometer is available to accurately measure ambient temperatures of cold holding equipment. Will follow-up on July 6, 2026 to see that the unit has a thermometer available.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

raw animal product over/with RTE food) Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Owners have switched to a ready to use disposable towel system with the sani-bucket, and quat product is now being used for the sani-bucket. Mostly dried out barely damp towel pulled from the container was observed at 100ppm quat. Another towel pulled from further down inside the bucket was closer to 150ppm, as was the small puddle of quat solution in the bottom of the container. Pre-mixed jug in the kitchen had a concentration of 400ppm, and label directions show required concentration of 200-400ppm. Based on information provided, the jug of pre-mixed solution and sani-bucket were both prepared as of the Saturday prior. Fresh solution was added to the sani-bucket, and management was advised to maintain the container of disposable towels and sanitizer the same way they would when they made bleach solutions. The quat solution needs to be refreshed daily and checked to verify concentration is at 200-400ppm as required by label use directions. Also, once wiping cloths are pulled up out of the container and lose moisture they will no longer be sanitizing surfaces. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Top layer of meatballs at front service hot holding had internal temperatures at 120F-128F, while meatballs further down were at 135F-140F. PIC noted they didn’t check the temperature prior to service this morning and could not verify heating temperature prior to beginning operations. Top layer of meatballs were removed and discarded. Meatballs were observed right around 135F-140F when checked again later. PIC was advised to ensure temperature checks prior to service to verify proper heating temperature and to stir frequently to maintain heat throughout entire product.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employees were observed washing hands without proper technique. Handles of manual faucet and paper towel dispenser were touched after handwashing was completed to shut off faucet and obtain paper towels for drying hands. Proper technique was discussed, and educational handout showing proper handwashing process was provided. Best practice would be to have paper towels ready prior to beginning handwashing process and use paper towels as a barrier after drying hands to shut off the manual faucet and touch the handle of the paper towel dispenser if additional towels need to be dispensed. Elbows and forearms may also be used to shut off the faucet and touch the handle to dispense paper towels. Ensure proper handwashing occurs between tasks and prior to food preparation and service. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Pizza screen used for toasting sandwiches was wiped with a sanitizer cloth and then dried with a napkin prior to placing it by the toaster oven for use. Wiping cloth was taken from a soiled sanitizer solution observed at 100ppm chlorine. Required concentration for bleach used is 200ppm. Proper cleaning and sanitizing of food contact surfaces between uses was discussed. All screens and trays were taken to dish area for ware washing. Ensure sanitizing solutions used to wipe toaster oven trays are maintained clean and at proper concentration and that trays are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use if proteins (meats/cheeses) and/or other TCS foods (lettuce/tomato) are present on food contact surfaces.
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

Solution was prepared earlier in the day and was discarded. Fresh solution at 200ppm was provided, and dishes were placed through ware washing process again to allow for proper cleaning and sanitization. Ensure bleach solutions are maintained at 200ppm and concentration is verified with test strips. 
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed quickly washing hands for less than 20 seconds. The faucet was shut off without a barrier, and the handle of the paper towel dispenser was touched to retrieve paper towels after process was completed. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and all staff working in the front service area re-washed hands properly. Educational handout on proper handwashing technique was provided.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
 To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11 Women's room handsink was observed to be extremely slow draining. As water was running the sink filled up and standing water remained for several minutes. Once water drained it was possible to see buildup in the grated drain cover. The buildup, which appeared to be mold, was causing the issue. A toothpick was used to clean out the drain cover holes enough to allow for proper drainage, and cleaner was poured down the drain. Clean the handsinks, including the drain covers, daily/as needed and make sure they are draining properly.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times.

A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 200ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

REPEAT> Observed the pre-packaged brownies and cookies to not have ingredients labels available. Provide ingredient and allergen labels for these pre-packaged baked goods. Since these are pre-packaged in advance of retail sale, they must have ingredient labels.
